title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck's letter to Tate (May 1966) on crystals, chapter 3, 'Remarks on p-divisible groups'. In 3.1 (previous page) he transposes Serre's construction (universal vector extension, as in Rosenlicht–Serre for abelian varieties) to a p-divisible group Phi over a base S on which p is locally nilpotent. Because Hom(Phi, formal G_a) = 0, there is a universal extension G(Phi) of Phi by the vector group of t_{Phi*}^vee. He conjectures that the relevant H^2/Ext sheaf is locally free of rank g* = dim Phi* and canonically isomorphic to Lie(Phi*), suggested by Lubin–Tate. The Lie algebra of G(Phi) is then an extension (*) 0 -> t^vee_{Phi*} -> H(Phi) -> t_Phi -> 0, the analogue of the Hodge filtration on de Rham H^1. He says G(Phi) varies 'less than Phi', but is not crystalline in general except perhaps to first order. Grothendieck–Messing theory later showed it is crystalline over nilpotent PD thickenings, so this hesitation was too pessimistic. This page continues as follows. (i) One should study the infinitesimal deformations of Phi once those of G(Phi) are fixed by a crystal in groups G. (ii) In 3.2, (*) is an interesting invariant. It extends by passage to the limit to Spec A, with A noetherian, J-adically separated and complete, and A/J of residue characteristic p; for instance A a complete DVR, possibly of mixed characteristic, with residue characteristic p. (iii) Special case: perfect residue field k, with Dieudonné module M over W of rank g+g* (typed g+g'). By the remark in 3.1, lifting the p-divisible group from k to A should be equivalent to lifting the Hodge filtration of M⊗_W k, given by (*), to a filtration of type (g,g*) on M⊗_W A. That is a deformation theory 'à la Hodge filtration', i.e. Grothendieck–Messing for the universal extension. (iv) He then asks for the Tate module of the generic fibre in terms of this datum (M, filtration on M⊗A). This is exactly the problem later called Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor' (ICM Nice 1970), solved by Fontaine's p-adic Hodge theory (Fontaine–Laffaille, crystalline comparison, Breuil, Kisin). (v) Finally he asks how much information the extension (*) carries for more general p-divisible groups, and notes that it plays the role of de Rham H^1.
errors: The claimed equivalence between lifts of the p-divisible group to a complete DVR A and lifts of the Hodge filtration to M⊗_W A is false in general. Grothendieck–Messing requires nilpotent divided-power thickenings; for A = O_K, A/m^n -> k carries such PD structures only when e <= p-1. Fontaine (Honda systems, 1977) proves a classification of this kind for e <= p-1. For e >= p, lifts are not classified by filtrations on M⊗A alone; one needs Breuil/Kisin modules.
The rank of M is written 'g+g'' and should read g+g* (height = dim Phi + dim Phi*).

The suggestion in 3.1 that G(Phi) is crystalline only to first order or in the toric/étale case is too pessimistic. Messing showed the universal extension is crystalline over nilpotent PD thickenings.
The conjectural local freeness and identification of the Ext sheaf with Lie(Phi*) is stated 'sauf erreur'. It is true (Messing 1972, Mazur–Messing 1974), but unproved here.

ideas.what: Universal vector extension of a p-divisible group, whose Lie algebra gives the Hodge filtration (*) as a substitute for de Rham H^1
ideas.modern_name: Universal extension / covariant Dieudonné crystal D(G) with Hodge filtration
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (ICM 1970); Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974)

ideas.what: Deformations of a p-divisible group from k to A correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration of the Dieudonné module
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory; Fontaine's Honda systems for e<=p-1

ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor' problem; crystalline comparison / Fontaine's D_cris, weakly admissible = admissible

missed.claim: This is an early (May 1966) explicit formulation of what Grothendieck publicly called the 'mysterious functor' problem in 1970: computing T_p of the generic fibre from the Dieudonné module plus a lifted Hodge filtration over a mixed-characteristic DVR. It is usually dated to the ICM 1970 talk. The letter to Tate is known to specialists (Messing, Illusie), so this is a dating and priority detail rather than a missed result.
missed.quote: Il serait bien intéressant d'essayer de déterminer, en termes d'une telle donnée, quel est le module de Tate correspondant à la fibre générique de φ !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historiography of p-adic Hodge theory: it pushes the origin of the crystalline comparison problem back to 1966, tied to the de Rham H^1 analogy.

deep.surprise_reason: Every idea on this page later became standard: Grothendieck–Messing theory, Fontaine's mysterious functor and p-adic Hodge theory. Its interest is the early 1966 date of the mysterious functor problem, together with an over-optimistic claim for arbitrarily ramified DVRs, in a letter that is already partly known to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '(de rang g+g' )' is in the typescript but mathematically should be g+g*
'réduit a la structure triviale' means 'réduit [i.e. the reduction over k] a la structure triviale'; a comma after 'formel' is added by hand
the struck-out text is 'un schéma formel noethérien'
at the end, 'qui remplac[e]' is cut off at the margin
'de φ' in line 1 is a struck/overtyped ∅ (Φ)
